page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-96 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the n1 family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 86.0 GB of system memory, which provides approximately 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show a significant performance divergence between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance, including stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests, falls into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance is strong, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark extended instructions tests ranking in the top 25%. Memory read bandwidth is also strong for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks, while write bandwidth and database operations perform in the average tier.

The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 0.9 GB per core represents a key tradeoff, making this instance less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory processing. However, it offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized, compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, parallel data processing, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
